title: Standardized counterparty risk scoring and conditional approval paths for enterprise redlines
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Sales and Legal spend too much time manually triaging MSA/DPA redlines for mid-market customers. There is inconsistent treatment of indemnity and liability concessions which increases cycle time and pricing leakage. Goal: introduce a standardized counterparty risk score and conditional approval paths to automate low-risk approvals and route higher-risk exceptions to the appropriate review queues (Legal, Security, Revenue Operations) with contextual recommendations for negotiation and pricing adjustments.

Scope: prototype a scoring model that combines: counterparty indicators (company size, industry, previous contract history), redline footprint (clauses touched: indemnity, liability cap, escrow), deal value (ARR), and security questionnaire flags. Expose score in the Sales UI and the Legal intake queue. Add conditional approval rules: auto-approve low-risk concession requests up to configured thresholds; require 1-stage Legal approval for medium risk; auto-escalate to Security/Head of Revenue for high risk.

Out of scope: full automation of bespoke enterprise amendments and previously blacklisted counteparties. Not replacing Legal judgment for strategic accounts.

Success metrics (initial): average contract turnaround time reduced by 25% in pilot accounts; number of auto-approved redlines without downstream exceptions <= 3% of approved deals; reduced manual Legal FTE hours on routine redlines by 20% in pilot.

Acceptance criteria: scoring prototype runs against last 12 months of contract telemetry (sample of >= 400 deals) and produces sensible risk bands; Sales UI surfaces score and recommended action; conditional rules can be toggled per-sales-segment and observed in audit logs; pilot roll out to 3 regional AE pods.

2026-02-27 - Liam O'Connor: Scoping review with Legal (Nadia Singh) and Security (Oliver Park). Agreed to include 'previous contract exceptions' as a negative signal. Noted trade-off: conservative scoring reduces auto-approvals but lowers false positives. Will start with conservative thresholds for pilot. Action: ENG to provide contract telemetry export (ENG-51888).

2026-03-03 - Legal (Nadia Singh): Reviewed clause mapping. Flagged three high-risk patterns we must always route: third-party indemnity transfer, uncapped consequential damages, and data escrow removal. Added as hard-stops in ruleset. Action: Add unit tests to rule engine.

2026-03-05 - Finance (Diego Ramos): Pricing experiment note: if auto-approval triggers, update quoting UI to show 'standard concession' badge and apply a standard discount holdback of 2% for liability increases > baseline. We will A/B test to measure revenue impact. Linked GA experiment: https://analytics.redwood.ai/experiments/contract-auto-approve-2026

2026-03-08 - ENG (Priya Patel): Initial telemetry export complete (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/compare/risk-telemetry). Found sparse SQ linkage for older deals; we will enrich with manual mappings for pilot. Also prototyped a simple logistic model (not prod) to validate signals.

2026-03-10 - PM (Maya Chen): Product decision: two-phase rollout. Phase 1 (Pilot): show score + recommendations (no auto-approve) to Sales and Legal for feedback. Phase 2: enable conditional rules for low-risk segments only after meeting QA gates. Added rollout checklist to Confluence.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Meeting notes with Legal and Sales Ops. Agreed KPIs, finalized pilot pods (NA-SMB, EU-Scale, APAC-Select). Security requires monthly review of audit logs.
